newsitem.title: USA: Mary Landrieu sworn in as senator from Louisiana.
newsitem.headline: Mary Landrieu sworn in as senator from Louisiana.

text.p: Democrat Mary Landrieu was sworn in Tuesday as a senator from Louisiana despite a challenge to her election last November by her Republican opponent Woody Jenkins.

Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott of Mississippi said Landrieu was sworn in without prejudice, meaning she could be removed from office by the Senate if an investigation finds she won because of fraud.

Landrieu beat Jenkins by less than 6,000 votes in the race to replace retiring Democrat Bennett Johnston. She was given her oath of office by Vice President Al Gore in the Senate chamber along with 33 other senators elected last November.

Jenkins has alleged Landrieu won because of widespread vote fraud. Asked by reporters about Jenkin's charges, Lott said, "Clearly, there appears to have been some improper things that happened on election day -- multiple voting, ghost voting, whatever.

"But I don't know how extensive it was, whether it would be enough to justify overturning the election," he said. "And I am going to proceed on the basis of letting the investigation be done in a bipartisan way and see what they come up with."

Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota said he was hopeful the investigation by the Senate Rules Committee would be objective and non-partisan. He said he was sure Landrieu would keep her seat.
Daschle noted that similar challenges were made and later dismissed against Democratic Sen. Dianne Feinstein of California and Republican Sen. Paul Coverdale of Georgia.
